items.title: Item 1
items.text: GOOG and BX Push AI With New Company *************************************** The WSJ reports Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG ) and Blackstone (NYSE:BX ) have announced the launch of a joint AI venture, with Blackstone providing an initial $5 billion of equity investment, as Wall Street continues to deepen ties with the AI build-out race. * “This new company has enormous potential as it helps to meet the unprecedented demand for compute”: Jon Gray, president and COO of Blackstone, explained the tie-up will allow customers to access Google Cloud’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), alongside offering data center capacity and related operations. * Investment in AI’s hard assets becomes increasingly appealing: As of the latest earnings, Blackstone has over $150 billion in data-center assets, with Alphabet inking regular deals expanding infrastructure. The new company aims to bring 500 megawatts of capacity online by 2027, a similar amount needed to power electricity for a midsize city. items.title: Item 2
items.text: INTC Makes Progress on Foundry Business ------------------------------------------ Intel (NASDAQ:INTC ) CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the manufacturing foundry business is gaining traction, being “one of the key national treasures,” as it continues to emerge as a key component of the turnaround plan. * “The best practice is to see 7% or 8% yield improvement per month, and now I’m seeing it”: Tan pointed out the improvements in the manufacturing process, with the yield (the percentage of usable chips from each wafer) now exceeding expectations. * “Tom believes that the market is completely missing the hidden value of Intel's manufacturing empire”: Back in March, Fool contributing analyst Rachel Warren discussed the company with TMF co-founder Tom Gardner, noting “Tom expects the real driver of the stock to be the Intel Foundry business as it becomes a massive, high-margin revenue engine.” Assess the foundry financials from Q1 ----------------------------------------------------------

items.title: Item 3
items.text: “The Strait of Hormuz Crisis is Not a Passing Headline” ---------------------------------------------------------- Yasser El-Shimy YASSER EL-SHIMY TEAM RULE BREAKERS The world's most important raw materials artery is closed and has been since late February. Nonetheless, the S&P 500 is around record highs. Those two facts seem irreconcilable – and yet here we are. But beneath the surface of those index highs, the tectonic plates of global trade are shifting … The ripple effects of this closure are about to wash over the global economy in ways the market appears determined not to price in. In this guide, we will work through the three questions that matter most to your portfolio right now: * How is this disruption actually working its way through the global economy? * Why is the market still so complacent? * And Then What? – what concrete steps can a Foolish investor take today to protect and position their portfolio for the turbulence ahead? items.title: Item 4
items.text: Next Up: Earnings and Data to Show Consumer Health ***************************************************** * Home Depot (NYSE:HD ) rose around 1% ahead of the opening bell, with the Dividend Investor rec beating analyst expectations for quarterly revenue and earnings. CFO Richard McPhail said “the homeowner in a relevant sense is perhaps more protected financially than other customer cohorts and so we continue to see engagement.” * CAVA Group (NYSE:CAVA ) releases earnings after the market closes. After posting a mixed bag last quarter , investors will be hoping for better same-store sales with recent menu changes. The stock is outperforming the S&P 500 by 46% since the October 2023 Rule Breakers rec. * U.S. pending home sales set to indicate continued growth: April data due at 10am E.T. is expected to show a 1.5% month over month (MoM) increase, matching the impressive 1.5% MoM increase from March, showing resilience in both the housing market and the general consumer. items.title: Item 5
items.text: Today’s Take: Learning the Hard Way ************************************** Tim Beyers In late 1999, I decided to parlay my interest in tech into a fresh position in shares of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN ). Co-founder Jeff Bezos had been named Time’s Person of the Year! Dumb idea. Amazon crashed, and I sold very near the bottom. I bought for the wrong reason (look at the hype!) and sold for the wrong reason (the stock is terrible, the business must be too!) — TIM BEYERS • TEAM RULE BREAKERS Here’s a sneak preview, but head to the article to reveal a stock you bought for the wrong reasons – and what you learned – or to submit questions to any of the featured analysts today! items.text: Your Take ************** YESTERDAY'S TOP RESPONSE We asked, year to date, would you say you’ve: Bought more stock than you’ve sold; Sold more stock than you’ve bought; Roughly an even split; or Mostly sat on your hands?
